clue.text: Man who's received everywhere

parts.note: a man's first name that radio operators the world over say to mean a message has been received

explanation.surface: A popular man is welcomed into every home.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a socially welcome guest; the trick is radio voice procedure, where this name is the word spoken to confirm a message got through.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure the name stands for 'received', so the man's name is heard wherever signals are acknowledged.

clue.text: Good writing is most to be trusted

parts.note: right means correct, good
hand means handwriting

explanation.surface: Neat handwriting suggests a reliable person.
explanation.walkthrough: A right-hand man is someone's most trusted helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of an assistant one relies on above all others, as in a chief deputy.

clue.text: In the Channel, use American compass

indicators.note: In puts the American abbreviation within the channel word

parts.note: a gut is a narrow channel or strait of water

explanation.surface: Crossing the English Channel, a navigator relies on a US-made compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass' looks like the navigator's instrument, but it means range; 'use' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of scope or full range, as in the whole spectrum of possibilities.

clue.text: Ordering a new border

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh frontier is being ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: This river forms much of the frontier between the US and Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: The river is a natural frontier between Texas and Mexico.

clue.text: Held and taken to court about blow

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second, holding it within

parts.note: someone taken to court has been sued
to blow money is to spend it

explanation.surface: Someone was detained and prosecuted after throwing a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a punch, but it is money blown, or spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hung up or kept in abeyance is held, as a sentence or payment can be held over.

clue.text: Army advanced, having received one signal

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army

indicators.note: having received means the money word takes in the numeral letter

parts.note: money advanced is lent
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Troops moved forward after getting a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' looks like a noun, but it is the adjective meaning notable; the answer's military sense, a forward bulge in a front, fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or prominent, as does a most noticeable point.

clue.text: Duke, trapped in sitting, kept quiet

indicators.note: trapped in shows the Duke abbreviation is enclosed by the sitting word

parts.note: sitting down means seated

explanation.surface: A nobleman was pinned in his seat and kept silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmed with a drug, so made tranquil and still.

clue.text: The standard very low score

explanation.surface: The usual score is very poor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman legions carried a bird figure as their standard; in golf this bird is two under par on a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman legion's emblem carried on a pole; also a golf hole finished two strokes under par.

clue.text: Girl's meeting Jack, perhaps; what a shame!

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a girl, with the 's
the jack is one of the honours, the top cards in bridge

explanation.surface: A girl takes up with Jack, which is a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the honours are ace, king, queen, jack and ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace or loss of respect, the state of being shamed.

clue.text: Refuse to read D Lawrence

parts.note: taken as written
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, enlisted in the RAF under the name Ross

explanation.surface: Someone declines to read the novels of D. H. Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'D Lawrence' suggests the novelist D. H. Lawrence; it is the D with T. E. Lawrence's assumed name.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun means rubbish or waste, the scum skimmed from metal.

clue.text: In speech, took a chance and skipped a bit

indicators.note: in speech means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: to take a chance is to gamble, past tense gambled

explanation.surface: Someone said they had taken a risk and left out part of their talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipped a bit' suggests omitting part of a speech, but it means frisked about playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic is to leap and skip about in play, as lambs do in spring.

clue.text: The chap to show relish

parts.note: Gus is a man's name, short for Augustus, so a chap

explanation.surface: A man proves he enjoys his food.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish here is enthusiastic enjoyment, a hearty zest for something.

clue.text: Train user starts to run coach

indicators.note: starts picks out the opening letter of each of the words Train and user

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A rail passenger's journey begins and a coach carriage is attached.
explanation.walkthrough: R for run is a cricket abbreviation from scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher who drills a pupil is a coach in the academic sense.

clue.text: Finally take one's turn, changing in private

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word take
changing tells us these letters swap places into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: At last someone takes a go at getting dressed behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' reads as getting changed in private, but it is the anagram signal for E plus ONESTURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English for 'between ourselves', said of something confidential.

clue.text: Opposed to profit, in a way

indicators.note: in places the profit word inside the letters made by a and way

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
to gain is to profit

explanation.surface: Someone is hostile to making money by any means.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition of opposition: being contrary to or hostile towards something.

clue.text: Notes to a composer are dry

parts.note: A and B are musical notes
Sir John Stainer was an English composer of church music

explanation.surface: Someone finds a composer's tunes dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' as a noun, chiefly American, is a supporter of prohibition, someone who drinks no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller who shuns alcohol, a prohibitionist in the American sense.

clue.text: Hector's a soldier

explanation.surface: The Trojan hero was a fighting man.
explanation.walkthrough: Hector looks like the Trojan prince, but as a verb it means to bully; ''s' is 'is' joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully or coerce someone into something; also a mounted infantryman of old cavalry regiments.

clue.text: Co-ordinates cases, bias being adjusted

indicators.note: being adjusted means the letters are shifted into a corrected order

explanation.surface: Legal cases are coordinated with prejudice corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: These are x-coordinates in geometry, measured along the horizontal axis.
explanation.definitionFit: In a graph, the horizontal distances of points from the vertical axis, a type of coordinate.

clue.text: Virgin Island, for example, is US territory

parts.note: virgin means new, unused
Jersey is an example of an island, one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: The Virgin Islands are an American possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin Island' suggests the US Virgin Islands; split it, Virgin is new and the island is Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of the USA on the Atlantic coast, so American land.

clue.text: Object is dispatched after the beginning of December

indicators.note: after puts the remaining pieces behind that opening letter
the beginning of December is its opening letter

parts.note: something dispatched has been sent

explanation.surface: A parcel goes out in early December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun, a thing posted, but it is the verb meaning to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to disagree or protest openly.

clue.text: A joint deposit made

indicators.note: made signals that the letters are formed into something else

explanation.surface: Two people make a shared bank deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like shared, as a joint account, but is a cut of meat: topside is a British cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean cut of beef from the upper leg, roasted as a Sunday piece of meat.

clue.text: "Scatter" appears in Webster's new edition

indicators.note: a new edition rearranges the material, so the letters of the dictionary name are reordered

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A word for spreading things about is listed in the latest dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Webster is a famous American dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning to strew things about, cover by sprinkling.

clue.text: Medical attendant of young girl put up in this town

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the whole run is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medical attendant
a deb, short for debutante, is a young girl entering society

explanation.surface: A doctor treating a young woman was given lodgings in this town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns DROFDEB around to give the town; it is the county town of Bedfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An English county town north of London.

clue.text: In the square Olive's dog is exemplary'

indicators.note: In means the fruit word sits inside the square word

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a square courtyard in a college
an olive is a drupe, a stone fruit; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Olive's pet dog in the town square behaves perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: Olive looks like a woman's name, but it is the fruit, botanically a drupe; 'is exemplary' says the dog is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-legged animal; a dog is a typical example.

clue.text: Whip head off syringe

indicators.note: head off removes the opening letter of the syringe word

parts.note: a squirt is a syringe or water pistol

explanation.surface: A whip knocks the end off a syringe.
explanation.definitionFit: A short riding crop with a braided leather lash, used in the American West.

clue.text: King, they say, takes heed

indicators.note: they say means the word is taken by how people pronounce it

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: Royalty is reportedly paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: An old verb, mostly in 'recks not', meaning to care or heed.
explanation.definitionFit: To reck is an archaic verb for to care or mind about something.

clue.text: One's girl coming out …

explanation.surface: Someone's daughter is making her debut.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to the next clue for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Children are a person's offspring, so a daughter counts; also an emergence or outflow.

clue.text: Steal money during party

indicators.note: during means the money letter falls within the party word

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or game
L stands for pound, a sum of money (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone pockets cash at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal' looks like theft, but it means to move stealthily, as in steal away.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep or edge along furtively, as one does when stealing into a room.

clue.text: - of Greece — from Heraklion, I conjecture

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A guess about something Greek, from someone in Crete's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Heraklion is the capital of Crete; the letters run across Heraklion, I and conjecture.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for Ionia, a Greek region, as in the classical order of columns.

clue.text: Edmund's cavalry

explanation.surface: The horsemen belonged to Edmund.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edmund II of England was nicknamed Ironside; Cromwell's Civil War cavalry were the Ironsides.
explanation.definitionFit: The English king Edmund's nickname in the possessive; also Oliver Cromwell's horse troopers.

clue.text: Not, so to speak, a Sultan

explanation.surface: A Sultan, put another way, is nothing of the kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not, so to speak' is a knot, sounded; a Turk's head is an ornamental knot. A Sultan heads the Turks.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative sailor's knot, spoken as 'not'; and a ruler of the Ottoman Empire as head of the Turkish people.

clue.text: Each single woman ready to lose heart

parts.note: Eve was the one and only woman in Eden

indicators.note: lose heart strips away the middle letters of ready, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Every unmarried woman is willing but becoming discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose heart' sounds like despair; it removes the middle of 'ready'.
explanation.definitionFit: A determiner meaning all of a group taken one by one.
